keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The range and quantity of tools included determines storage needs, budget, and complexity of the lending system.
Knowing who is organizing and managing this (one person, a committee, an HOA) shapes how responsibilities and authority are divided.
The physical location for storing and distributing tools — a garage, shed, community center — directly affects logistics and accessibility.
The available budget determines whether tools are donated, purchased, or both, and what tracking infrastructure is feasible.
How borrowers request, check out, and return tools — app, spreadsheet, honor system, in-person — defines the day-to-day operating model.
Whether this is informal and neighbor-run vs. a formally structured program with rules, liability waivers, and fees changes the entire tone and setup.
Defining what a successful launch looks like — number of members, tools borrowed per month, community engagement — sets the target to plan toward.

gold.taskDescription: Set up a community system where neighbors can borrow and return tools on a shared basis.

questions.title: Which types of tools are included in the library?
questions.description: Clarify the scope — hand tools only, power tools, garden equipment, ladders, etc. — and roughly how many items to start with.

questions.title: Who will run and manage the library day-to-day?
questions.description: Identify whether this is a solo effort, a small volunteer committee, or an existing group like an HOA or community association.

questions.title: Where will tools be physically stored and picked up?
questions.description: Determine the location — someone's garage, a shared shed, a community center — and how accessible it needs to be to neighbors.

questions.title: What is the budget for getting this started?
questions.description: Establish whether tools will be donated by neighbors, purchased new or used, or a mix — and what funds exist for shelving, signage, or software.

questions.title: How will borrowers check tools in and out?
questions.description: Decide on the tracking method — a shared spreadsheet, a lending app, a sign-up sheet, or an honor system — to define the operational workflow.

questions.title: Should this feel casual and neighborly or formally structured?
questions.description: Determine the tone and formality level — whether to include membership agreements, liability waivers, late fees, or keep it fully informal.

questions.title: What does a successful launch look like to you?
questions.description: Define the target outcome — a certain number of participating households, tools borrowed per month, or simply having the library open and running by a specific date.
